notes: EBIT is modeled using Carrier’s GAAP 'Operating profit' line from the consolidated financial statements. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

D&A and capex come from the consolidated statement of cash flows 'Depreciation and amortization' and 'Capital expenditures' lines as presented in Carrier’s FY2025 Form 10-K (with earlier-year comparability affected by portfolio reclassifications/discontinued operations presentation). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

NWC construction: (Accounts receivable, net + Inventories, net + Other assets, current) - (Accounts payable + Accrued liabilities), excluding cash, current debt, and assets/liabilities held for sale. Historical NWC is negative (payables-heavy). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318025000008/carr-20241231.htm))

Tax rate (DCF) is normalized to 0.20 to smooth historically volatile effective tax rates (e.g., FY2024 and FY2023 were elevated due to discrete items), while WACC (0.085) and terminal exit multiple (13.8x EV/EBITDA) are modeling assumptions consistent with peer multiple ranges. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318025000008/carr-20241231.htm))

catalysts: Riello divestiture timing through end of 1Q 2026 (regulatory approvals) and the follow-through on the guided sales/EPS headwind profile. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Sustained commercial HVAC + aftermarket momentum and any evidence that residential/light commercial weakness is stabilizing faster than assumed. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Execution of FY2026 share repurchases (~$1.5B) supporting per-share compounding relative to DCF intrinsic value. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Productivity initiatives and synergy capture (post-VCS acquisition) driving operating profit catch-up toward target margins. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))
company_overview: Carrier Global is a global provider of intelligent climate and energy solutions, offering digitally-enabled lifecycle solutions across heating, cooling, refrigeration, and building services. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Financial reporting is organized into Climate Solutions segments (Americas, Europe, Asia Pacific/Middle East & Africa, and Transportation). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Recent portfolio actions include the Viessmann Climate Solutions acquisition (completed Jan 2, 2024) and divestitures classified as discontinued operations in prior reporting periods. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))
current_context: Carrier guided for FY2026: sales around $22B with flat to low-single-digit organic growth (reported sales flat to up LSD) and an estimated ~$350M sales headwind from the Riello exit through timing. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

FY2026 adjusted operating profit is guided at ~$3.4B, with adjusted EPS of ~$2.80 and free cash flow of ~$2B. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Management also guided to about ~$1.5B in share repurchases for FY2026 and emphasized continued double-digit growth in global commercial HVAC and aftermarket, offset by weakness in residential/light commercial. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth is set to modest low-to-mid single digits, anchored to FY2026 guidance (flat to low-single-digit organic) and a gradual recovery profile through 2030. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Margin assumptions trend back toward an ~11% EBIT margin level, reflecting normalization after 2025 operating profit softness while staying conservative versus peak-adjusted metrics. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Capital intensity is modeled using historical D&A and capex as % of sales (forecast keeps D&A and capex ratios stable), supporting a steady conversion profile in the DCF. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Terminal value is driven by an exit EV/EBITDA multiple consistent with HVACR peer trading multiples (2026E proxies) to reflect a mature steady-state operating phase. ([clairfield.com](https://www.clairfield.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/HVACR-Industrials-Report-H2-2024.pdf))

Working capital is modeled as modestly negative (slightly payables-heavy) to reflect observed multi-year NWC behavior without overstating near-term cash inflows. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318025000008/carr-20241231.htm))
key_risks: Commercial demand softness or prolonged residential/light commercial weakness could keep EBIT margin below the recovery path. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Acquisition/integration and restructuring costs (including amortization of acquired intangibles) may weigh on GAAP operating profit. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Regulatory approval delays for Riello could extend the guided sales headwind window and complicate timing of cash flow normalization. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carrier-reports-2025-results-and-announces-2026-outlook-302680038.html))

Macro factors (FX, commodity/component costs) and working-capital volatility could shift cash conversion away from modeled NWC. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

presentation.subtitle: Carrier Global (CARR) — DCF + Comps Valuation Input Package (FY2023A–FY2030E Drivers)
valuation_summary: DCF base case chains from FY2025A net sales ($21.747B) using FY2026 guidance for reported sales scale (~$22B) and applies a controlled growth ramp into FY2030. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

EBIT margin and cash flow conversion use internally consistent operating profit, D&A, capex, and constructed NWC from audited statements. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1783180/000178318026000008/carr-20251231.htm))

Terminal assumptions use a Gordon/exiting framework via EV/EBITDA to align with industry valuation conventions observed in peer trading multiple disclosures. ([clairfield.com](https://www.clairfield.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/HVACR-Industrials-Report-H2-2024.pdf))
